notes: Replaced iam-policy-simulator-execution with iam-policy-simulator-source-ip-context and guardduty-archive-remediation with guardduty-suppression-keeps-detection to improve the distractors. Replaced vpc-longest-prefix-routing with vpc-static-route-propagated-priority to keep it distinct from the S3 gateway endpoint routing fact.

cards.statement: A matching explicit Deny in a role's permissions boundary overrides resource-policy access granted to its session ARN.
cards.explanation: A resource policy can grant permissions directly to an IAM role session, but an applicable explicit denial in the role's permissions boundary still blocks access.

source.title: Permissions boundaries for IAM entities

cards.statement: An IAM permissions boundary can grant its listed Allow permissions when the operator attaches it to a role.
cards.explanation: A permissions boundary sets a ceiling for identity-based permissions. Attaching the boundary grants no permissions by itself.
cards.misconception: Attaching a permissions boundary grants the role the actions that the boundary allows.

source.title: Permissions boundaries for IAM entities

cards.statement: A role trust policy can delegate role assumption to another AWS account by allowing that account's root ARN.
cards.explanation: An account root ARN names the trusted account, rather than just its root user. The account's administrators grant role-assumption permission to its IAM identities.

source.title: AWS JSON policy elements: Principal

cards.statement: An IAM password expiration policy revokes a user's active access keys when the password expires.
cards.explanation: IAM password expiration affects console sign-in. An IAM user can continue making programmatic requests with active access keys after the password expires.
cards.misconception: Expiration of an IAM console password also invalidates the user's access keys.

source.title: Set an account password policy for IAM users

cards.statement: With its zone of trust set to the account, IAM Access Analyzer trusts other accounts in the same organization.
cards.explanation: An external access analyzer scoped to an account trusts that account's principals. Principals in another organization member account remain outside its zone of trust.
cards.misconception: An account-scoped external access analyzer automatically extends trust to the account's organization.

source.title: IAM Access Analyzer findings

cards.statement: The IAM policy simulator automatically uses the requester's IP address to evaluate aws:SourceIp conditions.
cards.explanation: Operators supply aws:SourceIp as simulation input. The IAM policy simulator evaluates that supplied value rather than obtaining an IP address from a production request.
cards.misconception: The IAM policy simulator automatically fills aws:SourceIp from the caller's live request context.

source.title: IAM policy testing with the IAM policy simulator

cards.statement: A CloudTrail event history search returns management events from the AWS Region that the operator selects.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail event history searches cover an account within a selected Region. Operators inspect another Region separately when auditing activity there.

source.title: Working with CloudTrail event history

cards.statement: In AWS Organizations, SCPs attached to the organization root restrict IAM roles in the management account.
cards.explanation: SCPs leave users and roles in the AWS Organizations management account unaffected. Attaching an SCP to the organization root does not remove this exemption.
cards.misconception: An SCP attached to the organization root also restricts IAM roles in the management account.

source.title: Service control policies (SCPs)

cards.statement: In AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center automatically creates IAM roles for assigned permission sets.
cards.explanation: Assigning account access through a permission set makes IAM Identity Center provision corresponding roles in the assigned accounts, with the permission set's policies.

source.title: Manage AWS accounts with permission sets

cards.statement: AWS Trusted Advisor's Security Groups – Specific Ports Unrestricted check evaluates only IPv4 inbound rules.
cards.explanation: This Trusted Advisor check evaluates IPv4 ingress rules. Operators review IPv6 ingress separately rather than treating its result as an IPv6 exposure assessment.
cards.volatilityNote: Trusted Advisor check coverage may expand; the current check evaluates IPv4 inbound rules.

source.title: Security checks: Security Groups – Specific Ports Unrestricted

cards.statement: In AWS Organizations, AWS Config scopes conformance pack deployment to the Region of the deployment request.
cards.explanation: Organization conformance pack deployment is regional. Operators issue separate deployment requests in additional Regions to establish the pack there.

source.title: Managing Conformance Packs for AWS Config Across all Accounts in Your Organization

cards.statement: In AWS Organizations, an enabled AWS Control Tower detective control evaluates unenrolled accounts in its OU.
cards.explanation: Control Tower detective controls apply to enrolled accounts in a registered OU. Accounts in that OU that remain unenrolled fall outside those controls.
cards.misconception: OU membership alone brings an account under an enabled Control Tower detective control.

source.title: Detective controls

cards.statement: Amazon Macie creates a new finding when a later discovery run detects sensitive data in the same S3 object.
cards.explanation: Repeated discovery of sensitive data in the same S3 object produces a separate sensitive data finding. Macie treats subsequent discoveries as new findings.

source.title: Types of Macie findings

cards.statement: An IAM policy can grant access to an AWS KMS key independently of that key's key policy.
cards.explanation: An IAM policy's Allow has an effect on KMS key access when the key policy enables IAM policies. The default key policy includes that delegation.
cards.misconception: An IAM Allow grants KMS key access regardless of whether the key policy enables IAM policies.

source.title: Key policies in AWS KMS

cards.statement: AWS KMS can automatically select older key material to decrypt ciphertext created before that key's rotation.
cards.explanation: AWS KMS uses the key material that originally encrypted the ciphertext. Rotating the key material preserves decryption of earlier ciphertext.

source.title: Rotate AWS KMS keys

cards.statement: ACM rechecks public DNS validation CNAME records when renewing an in-use DNS-validated certificate.
cards.explanation: ACM checks that the certificate is in use and that its validation CNAME records resolve publicly. Keeping those records in place supports managed renewal.

source.title: Renewal for domains validated by DNS

cards.statement: ACM automatically renews an imported certificate when an operator associates it with an Application Load Balancer.
cards.explanation: ACM provides no managed renewal for imported certificates. Operators obtain a renewed certificate from its issuer and import the replacement.
cards.misconception: Associating an imported certificate with an AWS service makes it eligible for ACM managed renewal.

source.title: Import certificates into AWS Certificate Manager

cards.statement: AWS Secrets Manager's alternating users template keeps clone permissions after the original user's permissions change.
cards.explanation: Secrets Manager clones the original user's permissions during initial rotation. Later permission changes to the original user require operators to update the clone separately.

source.title: Lambda function rotation strategies

cards.statement: AWS Secrets Manager can rotate a replica secret independently while its replication link remains active.
cards.explanation: Secrets Manager rotates the primary secret and propagates its new value to associated replicas. Independent rotation requires promoting a replica to a standalone secret.
cards.misconception: An active replica secret has a rotation schedule independent of its primary secret.

source.title: Replicate AWS Secrets Manager secrets across Regions

cards.statement: Parameter Store read access to a SecureString parameter also grants decryption access to its customer managed KMS key.
cards.explanation: Reading a decrypted SecureString value requires kms:Decrypt permission on its encryption key in addition to Parameter Store read access.
cards.misconception: Permission to retrieve a SecureString parameter supplies the separate KMS decryption authorization.

source.title: Restricting decryption of SecureString parameter values

cards.statement: AWS Security Hub CSPM requires AWS Config recording to generate most security control findings.
cards.explanation: Most Security Hub CSPM controls use AWS Config service-linked rules. Enable AWS Config and record the relevant resources for those controls to produce findings.

source.title: Introduction to AWS Security Hub CSPM

cards.statement: AWS Security Hub can express exposure findings in the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).
cards.explanation: AWS Security Hub generates exposure findings using OCSF. Operators use that schema when consuming or analyzing these findings.

source.title: Introduction to AWS Security Hub

cards.statement: A suppression rule makes Amazon GuardDuty automatically stop generating findings that match its criteria.
cards.explanation: GuardDuty continues generating findings that match a suppression rule. The rule automatically archives those findings rather than stopping their detection.
cards.misconception: A suppression rule turns off detection for the finding criteria it matches.

source.title: Suppression rules in GuardDuty

cards.statement: With continuous scanning, Amazon Inspector waits for another push to check an eligible ECR image for new CVEs.
cards.explanation: Amazon Inspector rescans eligible images when it adds a relevant CVE to its vulnerability database. A new image push is unnecessary for that rescan.
cards.misconception: Inspector's continuous image scanning still needs another push before checking newly added vulnerabilities.

source.title: Scanning Amazon Elastic Container Registry container images with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: For identical destination CIDRs, a VPC route table prefers a static route over a propagated VPN route.
cards.explanation: When destination CIDRs match, a static VPC route takes priority over a route propagated from a virtual private gateway.

source.title: How route priority works

cards.statement: An EC2 security group can admit replies to an allowed inbound TCP connection despite restrictive outbound rules.
cards.explanation: Security groups track permitted connections. Reply traffic for an allowed inbound connection passes the security group regardless of its outbound rules.

source.title: Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups

cards.statement: A VPC network ACL applies a matching deny rule even when a lower-numbered rule allows the same inbound traffic.
cards.explanation: A network ACL evaluates rules from the lowest rule number and applies the first match. A later deny rule does not override an earlier matching allow rule.
cards.misconception: Network ACL deny rules take precedence over matching allow rules regardless of rule order.

source.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists

cards.statement: In automatic mode, a regional NAT gateway automatically expands across Availability Zones with VPC network interfaces.
cards.explanation: A regional NAT gateway in automatic mode tracks the VPC's network interface footprint and expands across supported Availability Zones as workloads appear.
cards.volatilityNote: Regional NAT gateways are a recent service capability whose expansion behavior may evolve.

source.title: Regional NAT gateways for automatic multi-AZ expansion

cards.statement: An S3 gateway endpoint route takes matching traffic ahead of a default route to a zonal NAT gateway.
cards.explanation: Requests selected by the S3 gateway endpoint route use the endpoint rather than the default zonal NAT route. Those requests avoid NAT processing.

source.title: Gateway endpoints

cards.statement: An interface VPC endpoint policy replaces its security group's inbound rules for service connectivity.
cards.explanation: An endpoint policy controls access to service operations and resources. The endpoint network interface's security group separately controls incoming network traffic.
cards.misconception: Authorizing service access through an endpoint policy also supplies inbound network access.

source.title: Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint

cards.statement: An active VPC peering connection supports routing onward through its peer's other peering connections.
cards.explanation: VPC peering carries traffic between directly paired VPCs. A peer VPC does not provide transit onward through another peering connection.
cards.misconception: Routes through an intermediate VPC make peering connections transitive.

source.title: How VPC peering connections work

cards.statement: A virtual private gateway distributes AWS Site-to-Site VPN egress traffic across equal-cost tunnel paths.
cards.explanation: A virtual private gateway selects a primary VPN tunnel for egress traffic. Equal-cost multipath routing is unavailable for Site-to-Site VPN connections on that gateway.
cards.misconception: Equal-cost VPN tunnels let a virtual private gateway distribute egress traffic across them.

source.title: Route tables and AWS Site-to-Site VPN route priority

cards.statement: Amazon VPC IPAM reports an overlap conflict for VPC CIDRs in different private scopes when their ranges intersect.
cards.explanation: Separate IPAM private scopes represent isolated address spaces. Operators can reuse private CIDRs across unconnected networks in different scopes.
cards.misconception: IPAM detects private address conflicts across its separate private scopes.

source.title: How IPAM works

cards.statement: With a DNS Firewall rule group associated, Route 53 Resolver passes queries through during firewall failure by default.
cards.explanation: With a DNS Firewall rule group associated, the default failure mode is closed. Route 53 Resolver returns SERVFAIL when DNS Firewall fails to reply.
cards.misconception: DNS Firewall defaults to allowing queries through during an evaluation failure.

source.title: DNS Firewall VPC configuration

cards.statement: In a web ACL, AWS WAF can still block a request after an earlier matching rule takes the Count action.
cards.explanation: Count records a rule match and continues evaluation. A later rule or the web ACL's default action can block a request already counted by an earlier rule.

source.title: Using rule actions in AWS WAF

cards.statement: Operators can route subnet traffic through AWS Network Firewall by targeting its endpoint in VPC route tables.
cards.explanation: After creating a firewall, operators update VPC route tables to send the traffic they want inspected through its firewall endpoints.

source.title: VPC route table configuration for AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: Creating a Route 53 private hosted zone automatically associates the account's other VPCs in that Region.
cards.explanation: VPC associations control which VPCs resolve the zone's records through their local Resolver. Creating the zone leaves the account's other VPCs available for explicit association.
cards.misconception: Creating a private hosted zone grants private DNS resolution to other VPCs in the same account and Region.

source.title: Working with private hosted zones

cards.statement: A Route 53 alias A record can point the hosted zone's apex to an Application Load Balancer.
cards.explanation: Route 53 permits an alias A record at the zone apex to target an Application Load Balancer, letting the root domain resolve to the load balancer.

source.title: Choosing between alias and non-alias records

cards.statement: With health checks on each record, Route 53 considers zero-weight records when all nonzero-weight records are unhealthy.
cards.explanation: In a health-checked weighted group, Route 53 turns to zero-weight records after the positive-weight records fail their checks. A healthy zero-weight record can then answer queries.
cards.volatilityNote: This card depends on the configured numeric weight zero; routing behavior may change.

source.title: Weighted routing

cards.statement: For unmapped client IP addresses, Amazon Route 53 selects the nearest configured geolocation record.
cards.explanation: A default geolocation record handles queries from IP addresses that Route 53 cannot map to a location. Without that default, Route 53 returns no answer for those queries.
cards.misconception: Unmapped client IPs fall back to the geographically nearest configured geolocation record.

source.title: Geolocation routing

cards.statement: Route 53 assumes a multivalue answer record is healthy when the operator leaves its health check unassigned.
cards.explanation: A multivalue answer record with no associated health check counts as healthy. Route 53 uses that assumed health when choosing records for DNS answers.

source.title: Multivalue answer routing

cards.statement: With public DNS query logging enabled, Route 53 can send query logs directly to an Amazon S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: Route 53 delivers public DNS query logs to CloudWatch Logs. Operators can export those logs from CloudWatch Logs to Amazon S3.
cards.misconception: Route 53 public query logging delivers directly to an S3 bucket.

source.title: Public DNS query logging

cards.statement: For DNS forwarding over Site-to-Site VPN, on-premises resolvers target Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint IPs.
cards.explanation: On-premises DNS resolvers forward applicable queries to the inbound endpoint's private IP addresses. The VPN provides a network path to those addresses.

source.title: Forwarding inbound DNS queries to your VPCs

cards.statement: When associated rules for a domain and its subdomain both match, Route 53 Resolver uses the subdomain rule.
cards.explanation: Resolver chooses the rule with the more specific matching domain. A matching subdomain rule takes precedence over its parent-domain rule.

source.title: How VPC Resolver determines whether the domain name in a query matches any rules

cards.statement: For SSE-KMS objects in an S3 origin, CloudFront OAC requires a KMS key policy granting the distribution access.
cards.explanation: The KMS key policy grants the CloudFront service principal permission to use the key for the specified distribution's SSE-KMS objects.

source.title: Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin

cards.statement: For an origin in Europe (Ireland), CloudFront uses a viewer certificate from ACM in Europe (Ireland).
cards.explanation: CloudFront uses ACM certificates from US East (N. Virginia) for viewer HTTPS, regardless of the origin's Region.
cards.misconception: A CloudFront viewer certificate in ACM belongs in the same Region as the origin.

source.title: Requirements for using SSL/TLS certificates with CloudFront

cards.statement: A CloudFront origin request policy can add selected viewer cookies to the cache key independently of a cache policy.
cards.explanation: An origin request policy forwards selected cookies to the origin. The cache policy separately determines which cookies form part of the cache key.
cards.misconception: Cookies selected in an origin request policy also become part of CloudFront's cache key.

source.title: Control origin requests with a policy

cards.statement: AWS Global Accelerator releases an accelerator's assigned static IP addresses when an operator disables the accelerator.
cards.explanation: Assigned IP addresses remain with an accelerator while it exists, including while disabled. Deleting the accelerator releases its assigned addresses.
cards.misconception: Disabling an accelerator releases its assigned addresses as deleting it does.

source.title: How AWS Global Accelerator works
